desks.Dividends: Apple, ex Thu Nov 12 at $0.27 per quarter (unchanged), and Microsoft, ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 (up from $0.91, +7.7%, its 24th consecutive annual increase), are the two capture dates in the window. No Nvidia, SPY, or QQQ ex-dates fall in the window, and Tesla pays no dividend.
desks.Earnings: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in-window, Tue Nov 17 after close (call 5:00 p.m. ET), with Nasdaq consensus EPS of $2.49. Apple reported Mon Nov 2 after close with revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% year over year, and EPS of $2.10; its first-session reaction was -1.9% on Nov 3, followed by +5.3% on Nov 4. Microsoft reported Oct 28 and Tesla reported Oct 21.
desks.Futures: The EIA petroleum report landed on schedule today with crude, gasoline, and distillate all drawing, distillates at a 23-year low, yet crude sold off about 7-9% on midterm results and Iran de-escalation hopes. Gulf exports averaged 17.1 million barrels per day in October, down from 18.9 in September. Next catalysts in order: EIA gas storage Thu Nov 5, USDA WASDE Tue Nov 10.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found for the watchlist. Okta replaces Kenvue in the S&P 500 before the open today, a mechanical acquisition-driven constituent swap, not a parity signal. The S&P style-index methodology revision, with pro forma files Dec 4 and effective Dec 21, changes growth/value classification, not S&P 500 membership, and is a watch item only.
desks.Premium: Live next-expiry implied volatility prints are SPY about 11-12%, QQQ about 20-23%, Apple about 23-27%, Microsoft about 25-30%, Nvidia about 39-45%, and Tesla about 41-47%. Nvidia's 37-day print of 45.08% spans the Nov 17 earnings date and is earnings-contaminated. SPY has no clean verdict: a single day drives 32.5% of 20-day realized variance, over the 30% line, so the SPY read is WINDOW-CONTINGENT. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names, and front-week index call/put volatility gaps on post-close marks most likely reflect stale quotes.
desks.Quant lab: No new candidate was added and there was no TEST or INTEGRATE movement. One item reopened: Buchegger and Gonon on arbitrage-aware probabilistic forecasting of implied volatility surfaces moved from ARCHIVE back to WATCH (score 56) after a code link appeared in the paper itself, but repo contents, license, and licensed-data replication remain unverified. Its honest headline is that it beats persistence only beyond about weekly horizons and still loses at 1 day, with predictive intervals too narrow.

headline: Daily research brief — Wednesday, November 4

items.detail: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in the window, Tue Nov 17 after close, with Nasdaq consensus EPS of $2.49, confirmed by the company release, the Nasdaq calendar, and Zacks. The Nov 20 expiry straddle implies about 9.0%, against a vendor stripped estimate of 7.3% and a last earnings-day move of +8.7% on Aug 27. The 37-day implied volatility of 45.08% spans the Nov 17 date, so it is an earnings-contaminated quote, not a clean volatility level.
items.title: Nvidia reports Nov 17, and premium into the print is an avoid

items.detail: The EIA report released today at 10:30 a.m. ET showed crude down 865,000 barrels, gasoline down 222,000, and distillates down 3.565 million to 99.3 million, the lowest since May 2003, yet Brent broke below $100 and WTI traded about $88.50 to $91.80 late. Per Reuters coverage, midterm results and Iran de-escalation hopes drove the selloff. The claim that Hormuz could reopen within 2 days is single-source and UNVERIFIED, and Gulf exports stayed depressed at 17.1 million barrels per day in October, down from 18.9 in September.
items.title: Crude sold off into bullish inventory data — a war-premium unwind, not a glut signal

items.detail: FRED prints dated Nov 3, the latest available, put the effective fed funds rate at 3.88%, the 2-year at 4.61%, and the 10-year at 4.95%, a 2s10s spread of +34 basis points, about 7 basis points flatter than 60 days ago. Both ends have retraced from window highs of 5.31% on the 10-year and 4.92% on the 2-year. SOFR at 3.97% sits 9 basis points over the effective fed funds rate, a normal overnight funding print with no stress signal. Near 5%, the 10-year remains a valuation headwind for long-duration names on discount-rate grounds.
items.title: Rates: 10-year at 4.95%, curve sloping up and flattening, funding calm

items.detail: Microsoft goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 per quarter, up from $0.91, a 7.7% increase announced Sep 15 and its 24th consecutive annual increase under the desk standard, payable Dec 10. Apple goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 12 at $0.27, unchanged from August, declared with the Nov 2 earnings release and payable Nov 16. No cuts or specials were announced on the watchlist, and Tesla pays no dividend.
items.title: Two dividend dates in the window, one of them a raise
